title: Finite root site comparison with scalar and scheme coherence
statement:
Let $m\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $mA=0$, and let $T$ be a scheme on which $m$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]. On the small etale and pro-etale sites use their comparison $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}}$ for the etale sheaf of units $z$ with $z^m=1$ [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] and $\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}$ for the same root functor on weakly etale tests [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Put $E_{m,T}=\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/m)_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}}A_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}$ and $D_{m,T}=\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/m)_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}}A_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}$.

There are canonical $(\mathbf Z/m)$-linear and $A$-linear isomorphisms
$$c_{m,T}:\nu_T^{-1}\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{pro}},\qquad \sigma_{m,T}:\nu_T^*E_{m,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{m,T}.$$
For every weakly etale $f:W\to T$, identify $(\nu_T^{-1}\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}})(W)$ with $\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{et}},f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}})$ and then with $\{z\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)^\times:z^m=1\}$. Under this identification $c_{m,T}$ sends a root to that same unit. The map $\sigma_{m,T}$ is the canonical balanced-tensor comparison followed by $c_{m,T}\otimes1$, with constant scalars unchanged. Equivalently, for an etale $U\to T$, a pro-etale test $W\to T$, and a $T$-map $f:W\to U$, the comparison-adjunction unit sends a local tensor $z\otimes a$ on $U$ to a section whose restriction to $W$ is carried by $\sigma_{m,T}$ to $f^\sharp(z)\otimes a$.

For every $v:T'\to T$, let $e^v_m:v_{\mathrm{et}}^*E_{m,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{m,T'}$ be the etale root-tensor pullback along the etale inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and let $d^v_m:v_{\mathrm{proet}}^*D_{m,T}\to D_{m,T'}$ be induced by the canonical pro-etale root map adjoint to pullback of units [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Under the canonical comparison square [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] $\kappa_v:v_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\nu_T^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\nu_{T'}^*v_{\mathrm{et}}^*$ one has
$$d^v_m\,v_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\sigma_{m,T}=\sigma_{m,T'}\,\nu_{T'}^*(e^v_m)\,\kappa_v.$$
In particular $d^v_m$ is invertible. These equations, and the corresponding root-only equations for $c_{m,T}$, respect identities and composites. For $m\mid m'$ with $m'$ invertible on $T$, the root power map $z\mapsto z^{m'/m}$ commutes with $c_{m,T}$ and $\sigma_{m,T}$ (using the same $A$, killed by $m$), with the evident reductions of constant scalar rings. No affine, Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis on $T$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the existing Cartier root isomorphism and its kernel-inclusion equation. Evaluation preserves kernels; identify etale and pro-etale kernel sections with actual roots of unity. Compose these equivalences with the normalized etale root pullback to obtain root_sections. Transpose Cartier units comparison to prove root_unit, and use naturality for every restriction W to U.

source.place: Tag 03EL; scalar-extension adjunction, with proetale.tex Tag 0GLZ and canonical adjunction mates.

proof.text: Compose the sheafification adjunction, the sectionwise extension/restriction-of-scalars adjunction, and the equivalence between additive and Z/m-linear maps from roots. This gives natural Hom equivalences for the two root tensors. Combine them with comparison adjunction and the Cartier root isomorphism to define sigma. Precomposition by sigma is bijective on every Hom set, hence sigma is an isomorphism. The adjunction units give its generator equation; A-linearity and naturality give arbitrary scalars and restrictions.

source.place: Tag 03EL; scalar-extension adjunction, with proetale.tex Tag 0GLZ and canonical adjunction mates.

proof.text: Define d explicitly by transposing the recorded pro-etale root projection map through the scalar Hom equivalence and inverse-image adjunction. The generator equation follows from the two adjunction units. This construction does not require invertibility of m.

source.place: Tag 03EL; scalar-extension adjunction, with proetale.tex Tag 0GLZ and canonical adjunction mates.

proof.text: Transpose the inverse canonical comparison mate under the two composite adjunctions. The general unit equation for conjugate adjoints identifies this with postcomposition by the canonical right-image comparison. At every etale U, both root adjuncts pull a unit along the same fibre-product projection: use the Cartier inclusion equation, the recorded pro-etale root projection formula, and the normalized etale root inclusion law. Injectivity of the root inclusion and of adjunction proves root_square. Applying the scalar Hom equivalence, both tensor adjuncts have the same generator values by the normalized etale law and d_unit. This proves scheme_square. All other factors in that square are isomorphisms, proving d_isIso after pulling back the inverse of m.

source.place: Tag 03EL; scalar-extension adjunction, with proetale.tex Tag 0GLZ and canonical adjunction mates.

proof.text: The normalized etale tensor identity and composition laws, the canonical comparison coherence, and cancellation of the invertible sigma give d_id and d_comp. For roots, transpose the canonical identity and composition comparisons. Their right-image maps restrict along the identity and associativity maps of fibre products. The projection equations and functoriality of global sections identify the two root formulas, proving root_id and root_comp.

source.place: Tag 03EL; scalar-extension adjunction, with proetale.tex Tag 0GLZ and canonical adjunction mates.

proof.text: Take the normalized etale exponent-change q and tE. Define tP through the scalar Hom equivalence from the recorded pro-etale power transition, obtaining its generator formula. Postcompose the root power square by the monic inclusion into units. The q inclusion equation, the kernel-lift equation for the pro-etale transition, and integer linearity of Cartier comparison give equality. Transposing through the scalar Hom equivalence and comparison adjunction now proves the tensor power square. All calculations include exponent one, zero coefficients and the empty scheme.
